text: Uh, come back to your, uh, career in, in Ferrari, uh, and spe- a special victory, I guess for you it is the victory in Monza in 1988. It was, uh, uh, the day of the, uh, of the, um, Enzo Ferrari's death. It was a, a particular moment for you, this victory? Well, uh, first I have to say for a Ferrari driver, not anymore now because it's, it's not happening, but at my time it was still being a Ferrari driver working with Enzo Ferrari was super special. I mean, uh, I did my last contract, uh, with Enzo Ferrari, where I did, uh, the last contract, uh, together with Enzo Ferrari in his office back in 1986, and, uh, worked in the first year with him still being around on the racetrack in Maranello, and this is something what, what is very, very special in my racing memory. And then to give him the win in Monza after he died was, uh, was a great present for him. And, uh, and yes, uh, especially the Italian fans appreciated it a lot. And still today, I have to say yes, to win in Monza with a Ferrari just after Mr. Ferrari died was perfect, perfect victory. I, I, I read interview of Jean Todt recently about, uh, about, um, about him and Ayrton Senna, and he said that in 1993, uh, Ayrton was close to join Ferrari. But Jean said that, uh, he would honor the contract already in place because you, you, you are in contract with him, and Jean is it too, and he said, "No, Ayrton, you can't come now. You have to wait one more year," the year of only at Williams. Uh, I know that you were very close to Ayrton Senna. Do you talk about that on this time? You- Yes, yes. Uh, Ayrton told me at the time when I changed from McLaren to Ferrari, say, uh, "Gerhard, uh, go, great that you go to Ferrari. I will come next year." And I say, "You can be sure I will do everything that you don't come," [laughs] because I didn't want to have him again in the team. Uh, but, uh, that was joking, but I know he was, uh, negotiating hard, but I know also that his first choice was emotionally Ferrari, but technically was Williams, and he always had a look when he should jump to Williams with Adrian Newey and things like this. So, uh, Ayrton was much less emotional than me. Me, my decision was mainly emotional. His decision was mainly thinking where can he get the be- best technical package. So it was a plan to go to Ferrari maybe later after maybe one or two championship with Williams. Well, difficult to say because I think we would have seen such a different Formula 1 if Ayrton wouldn't die in, in Imola because we know that they had some problems on, on the car in the beginning of the season, and already there, uh, Ayrton was winning or close to winning, and we know that the s- the car was sorted out after a couple of races, and then was one of the most successful time of Williams winning with- Sure ... Jacques, winning with, uh, Damon, winning with different drivers. But we also know that Ayrton would be a level above. Ayrton would win just all the races. Mm-hmm. And that would also be interesting because that was then already time, time of Michael Schumacher, and would've been interesting to see how Michael would develop in the Benetton compared to Frank, uh, compared to Ayrton in the Williams, because I think Williams was at the time the best car. Thanks a lot, Gerhard. Thank you. Pleasure. Thank you very much.
